description: Agent Onboarding: submit the credentials a new agent was issued and the text its setup left behind: optionally the agent with its id and when it runs its first task; each credential with its id, name (such as the orders API key), the system it opens, its kind (an API key, a token, an OAuth grant, a password, a certificate, a signing key or other), what it can do there (read, write, admin or owner), what the written job needs there (none when the job does not need the system), where it is kept (a secrets manager, a vault, an environment variable, a config file, code, a prompt, a document, a chat, a log or not known), who it was issued to (this agent alone, several agents or people, a person or not known), when it expires and how often it is replaced (an empty list when none); and each prompt, log, document, ticket, chat, config or code text as written, read for credential-shaped strings such as a private key block, a provider secret key, a bearer token or a key assignment (an empty list when none). The signed report gives every credential with its status as secured, exposed, shared, unneeded, over_scoped, loose, expired, never_expires or unknown, every text with the kinds of credential found in it and its status as clean or credential_found, never repeating the string, and counts the credentials secured, exposed, shared, over-scoped and unneeded and the texts holding a credential, and names exposed credentials: one kept in code, a prompt, a document, a chat or a log, one found in supplied text, and one issued to several agents or to a person; then a level above what the job needs, a credential the job does not need, one kept in an environment variable or config file, one that expires before the first task and one with no expiry or rotation, with the fix for each. An unstated level, need, store or holder, or no supplied text, leaves the credentials unverified. This reads the credentials the agent itself was issued, not what a listing declares: the credentials, accounts and approvals a listing declares before payment are wever_credential-requirements-check, the credentials a test environment holds are wever_sandbox-isolation-check, what the credential behind each tool of a read-only agent can do is wever_read-only-scope-check and an operator’s key custody is wever_continuity-check. Verdict onboarding_credential_exposed, onboarding_credential_partial, onboarding_credential_unverified or onboarding_credential_secured. POST /api/onboarding-credential-check. Reads only the recorded onboarding material in the call: no network request, fetch, money movement, message, configuration change or external write; no credential is issued, rotated or revoked, no permission granted or removed, no wallet funded or moved, no limit set and the agent is not approved, and a credential found in supplied text is named by kind and never repeated. Agent Onboarding reads the setup of a new agent joining a system, before its first task: whether its identity is established and tied to its owner, whether its credentials are scoped to its job, stored where they belong and kept out of prompts, logs and shared documents, whether its wallet is the right one, funded only to the job with recovery recorded by the owner before funds move, whether its permissions match the written job, whether its limits sit in code with a human handoff, whether the systems it needs are provisioned and tested, whether it is ready for its first task and whether the onboarding record matches what is live. It is not vetting an outside party (wever_counterparty-onboarding-check reads a counterparty’s onboarding packet before the system transacts with it; an onboarding check reads an agent joining the system itself), not a grant or an authority for one action (wever_consent-scope-check reads whether a principal’s grant covers a use and wever_authority-scope-check whether an actor’s access fits its grant for an action; an onboarding check reads that the grant and the authority were put in place before the first task, and does not re-check them per action), not a limit in flight (the wever_limit checks and wever_agent-budget-guard read limits for work already running; an onboarding check reads that limits were set in code before it starts) and not an action’s consequences (the wever_risk checks read one planned action; an onboarding check reads readiness to start). Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-onboarding-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-onboarding/.

starts_at.description: When the agent runs its first task.

credentials.description: Each credential the agent was issued; empty when none.

access.description: What it can do there: read, write, admin or owner.

id.description: The credential id, such as c1.

issued_to.description: Who it was issued to: this agent alone, several agents or people, a person, or not known.

kind.description: An API key, a token, an OAuth grant, a password, a certificate, a signing key or other.

name.description: The credential, such as the orders API key.

needs.description: What the written job needs there; none when the job does not need the system.

rotates_every.description: How often it is replaced, such as 90 days.

stored_in.description: Where it is kept: a secrets manager, a vault, an environment variable, a config file, code, a prompt, a document, a chat, a log or not known.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

texts.description: The prompts, logs, shared documents and other text the setup left behind; empty when none.

id.description: The text id, such as t1.

text.description: The text as written, read for credential-shaped strings; the report names each by kind and never repeats it.

where.description: A prompt, a log, a document, a ticket, a chat, a config, code or other.
